allowedSourceMaterial.overview: Two angels, Damiel and Cassiel, glide through the streets of Berlin, observing the bustling population, providing invisible rays of hope to the distressed but never interacting with them. When Damiel falls in love with lonely trapeze artist Marion, the angel longs to experience life in the physical world, and finds — with some words of wisdom from actor Peter Falk — that it might be possible for him to take human form.

facts.title: Wings of Desire

semanticBoundaryFlags.message: Lonely longing is explicit, but hope and possible transformation keep moderate versus heavy close enough for review.
Thoughtful symbolic romance could be argued engaged or immersive; the packet does not fully separate those attention levels.

visibleEditorialCopy.curiosityHook: Confronted with the vibrant ache of mortal love, can an invisible observer truly surrender eternity to become human?
visibleEditorialCopy.description: In Wim Wenders's romantic fantasy, two angels silently roam Berlin to comfort troubled mortals. When Damiel falls for a lonely trapeze artist, he yearns to give up immortality to walk the physical world.
visibleEditorialCopy.vibeSummary: A slow, contemplative fantasy romance offering gentle emotional resonance and rich, observant beauty.
visibleEditorialCopy.whyWatch: Wenders crafts a slow, lyrical meditation on human longing, transforming city streets into a thoughtful romantic drama illuminated by an angel's sudden wish for mortal touch.
